definitions.explanation: A state of harmonious, well-balanced proportions. Most commonly used to describe physical bodies, architecture, and other visual forms that are pleasing due to their balanced proportions.

examples.japanese: {均整|きんせい}のとれた{体|からだ}。
この{建物|たてもの}は{均整|きんせい}が{美|うつく}しい。
{彫刻|ちょうこく}の{均整|きんせい}のとれたフォルムに{見入|みい}ってしまった。
examples.english: I found myself gazing at the well-balanced form of the sculpture.

notes:
Composed of {均|きん} (equal, level) + {整|せい} (order, arrangement). Describes the visual harmony that comes from balanced proportions.

USAGE:
{均整|きんせい} is most commonly encountered in the set phrase {均整|きんせい}のとれた (well-proportioned, well-balanced). It is a literary and descriptive word, used in writing about art, architecture, the human body, and aesthetics. It implies visual balance and harmony rather than mere symmetry.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {均整|きんせい}のとれた: well-proportioned, well-balanced
- {均整|きんせい}のとれた{体型|たいけい}: well-proportioned figure
- {均整|きんせい}{美|び}: beauty of proportion
- {均整|きんせい}を{保|たも}つ: to maintain proportion

SIMILAR WORDS:
- バランス: balance — a common loanword used broadly for balance in any domain
- {対称|たいしょう}: symmetry — specifically mirror symmetry, more geometric than {均整|きんせい}
- {調和|ちょうわ}: harmony — broader concept of things fitting together well, not limited to visual proportion
